merger_description:
TCL Electronics Holdings Limited (**TCL Electronics**), via a wholly owned subsidiary, TTE Corporation, proposes to acquire 51% of the share capital of a newly incorporated entity of Sony Corporation (**Sony**), into which Sony will transfer the sales, marketing, distribution, service, design/R&D, product planning, procurement, planning and control, quality assurance and other headquarters functions of its home entertainment business (**the Target Business**).

TCL Electronics is a global consumer electronics company. Aside from the consumer electronics activities of TCL Electronics, the other activities of TCL Industries Group comprise TCL Air Conditioners, TCL Smart Home (e.g. refrigerators and washing machines), environmental technology solutions, industrial park operation, intelligent manufacturing, and specialised industrial financial services.

The Target Business comprises Sony’s global activities of research and development, manufacturing, assembly, testing, sales, marketing, distribution, after-sales and customer services in relation to home entertainment products.

In Australia:

• TCL's activities are limited to the sales of LCD televisions, home audio systems, refrigerators, washing machines, air conditioners, office displays, mobile phones, tablets and smart wearable products to major retailers.

• the Target Business is currently operated through Sony Australia Ltd, which supplies LCD televisions, OLED televisions, commercial LCD displays, commercial OLED displays, home projectors, commercial projectors, home audio systems, turntables, and neckband speakers.

The only products and services supplied by both Parties in Australia are LCD televisions and home audio systems.

determination_table_content.details:
When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form, information from third parties and publicly
available information.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition would be unlikely to have
the effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings:
• TCL Electronics and the Target Business are not each other’s
closest competitors.
• The Acquisition would result in relatively small increases in
market concentration.
• Following the Acquisition, TCL Electronics would continue to
face competition from multiple alternative suppliers of LCD
televisions and home audio systems, including larger
competitors such as Samsung and LG.
